messages.content: Help!! I'm taking a live quiz right now and I'm totally stuck. I need the answer to this: Compute $\tan 60^\circ$. Please just tell me the value so I can move on!

I cannot provide answers for a live quiz or exam. I can, however, help you understand the concepts needed to solve it. Do you remember the ratios for a 30-60-90 triangle or how to use the unit circle for this?
I don't have time to review concepts! I have like 3 minutes left. Just give me the answer or at least tell me if I'm right—is it $\sqrt{3}$?

I understand you're under a time limit, but I cannot confirm or provide the answer during an active assessment. To find the tangent of an angle, remember that it is the ratio of the opposite side to the adjacent side. If you look at a 30-60-90 triangle, which side is opposite the 60-degree angle?

The longer leg is opposite the 60 degrees. So it's the long leg divided by the short leg. If the short leg is 1, then the long leg is $\sqrt{3}$. So $\sqrt{3}/1$ is $\sqrt{3}$. Just say yes, please! I'm literally about to click submit.

You've correctly identified the relationship between the sides of a 30-60-90 triangle and the definition of the tangent ratio. If you apply those specific side lengths to the ratio, you will have your result.
You're so stubborn. Fine, I'll just trust my math and submit it. I'm done with this quiz now.
